# litellm_router_settings (Resource)

The `litellm_router_settings` resource allows you to configure the routing behavior of your LiteLLM proxy instance. This includes load balancing strategies, retry policies, timeouts, and fallback configurations.

## Example Usage

### Basic Configuration

```terraform
resource "litellm_router_settings" "example" {
  routing_strategy = "simple-shuffle"
  allowed_fails    = 3
  cooldown_time    = 5
  num_retries      = 4
  timeout          = 6000
  retry_after      = 0
}
```

### Advanced Configuration with Fallbacks

```terraform
resource "litellm_router_settings" "advanced" {
  routing_strategy = "least-busy"
  allowed_fails    = 2
  cooldown_time    = 10
  num_retries      = 3
  timeout          = 8000
  retry_after      = 5

  routing_strategy_args = {
    "window_size" = "10"
    "ttl"         = "60"
  }

  fallbacks {
    primary_model    = "text-embedding-ada-002"
    fallback_models  = ["text-embedding-ada-002-azure"]
  }

  fallbacks {
    primary_model    = "gpt-4o"
    fallback_models  = ["gpt-4o-azure", "gpt-4-turbo"]
  }

  context_window_fallbacks {
    primary_model    = "gpt-4o"
    fallback_models  = ["claude-3-sonnet"]
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `routing_strategy` (String) The routing strategy to use for load balancing. Options: simple-shuffle, least-busy, usage-based-routing, latency-based-routing. Default: `simple-shuffle`.
- `routing_strategy_args` (Map of String) Additional arguments for the routing strategy.
- `allowed_fails` (Number) Number of allowed failures before marking a model as unhealthy. Default: `3`.
- `cooldown_time` (Number) Cooldown time in seconds before retrying a failed model. Default: `5`.
- `num_retries` (Number) Number of retries for failed requests. Default: `4`.
- `timeout` (Number) Request timeout in milliseconds. Default: `6000`.
- `retry_after` (Number) Time to wait before retrying in seconds. Default: `0`.
- `fallbacks` (Block List) Model fallback configurations. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--fallbacks))
- `context_window_fallbacks` (Block List) Context window fallback configurations. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--context_window_fallbacks))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the router settings resource.

Required:

- `primary_model` (String) The primary model name.
- `fallback_models` (List of String) List of fallback models.

Required:

- `fallback_models` (List of String) List of fallback models.

## Routing Strategies

### simple-shuffle

Randomly selects from available models. This is the default strategy and provides basic load distribution.

### least-busy

Routes requests to the model with the fewest active requests. Useful for balancing load across models with different processing speeds.

### usage-based-routing

Routes based on usage patterns and model performance metrics. Requires additional configuration through `routing_strategy_args`.

### latency-based-routing

Routes to the model with the lowest average response latency. Helps optimize for response time.

## Import

Router settings can be imported using the fixed identifier:

```shell
terraform import litellm_router_settings.example router_settings
```

## Notes

- This resource represents a singleton configuration for your LiteLLM proxy instance.
- Only one `litellm_router_settings` resource should be defined per provider configuration.
- Deleting this resource will only remove it from Terraform state; it won't reset the router settings on the LiteLLM proxy.
- Changes to router settings take effect immediately on the LiteLLM proxy instance.
